You know

[Verse 1]  
Got my feet in your lap on a Tuesday, you’re scrolling, I’m stealing your hoodie,  
Take your fries then I sip on your shake, you just laugh, you don’t call it a mistake.  
Out where the dirt road ends and the creek runs slow,  
Boots and mud, coffee cups, tacos fallen, still we love.  

You remember the candy that I like, little things and you never get tired,  
Leave a note in the pocket of my coat, “Text me when you read this” in your tiny joke.  
I got rough rocks in my pockets, mud caked on my boots,  
Life spills over, we just drink it up.  

[Pre-Chorus 1]  
You say “Babe, you been working too hard,” pull me close, hide my phone in the car,  
Turn the lights down, put my hair up for me, order takeout, choose the dumb movie.  
Calloused hands from haulin’ hay, sun‑kissed skin that don’t bruise,  
Chocolate with a squeeze of citrus, velvet with a wink—oh God, those hands.  

[Chorus A x Chorus B]  
Spoil me a little, it feels so good,  
You know every craving better than I could,  
Don’t need diamonds, don’t need the world out there,  
Just spoil me a little, I know you care.  

He’s chocolate sweet with a sour spark,  
Golden honey with a question mark,  
Checks my pulse, steadies my spin,  
Won’t dive deep till he’s sure he can swim.  
If I’m sugar rushing through the dark,  
He’s the tart that wakes my heart.  

[Verse 2]  
You rub circles right into my palm, tell me stories just to keep me calm,  
Who knew comfort could feel like a dare to let somebody love me like this, so rare.  
He tastes like midnight melted slow, cocoa words in a gentle flow,  
Says “You okay?” like warm rain falls, wraps me up in caramel walls.  

But darlin’, underneath this grit, there’s a heart beatin’ proud,  
He’ll kiss my forehead, smooth my hair, ask what future we’re declaring there.  
Then night falls soft like rain on tin,  
Boots and mud, coffee cups, tacos on the pavement, we still show up, we still show up.  

[Pre-Chorus 2 – DJ Drop]  
He’s velvet voice and careful hands,  
Drawing maps before he lands,  
Sugar steady, citrus bright,  
Soft by day, sharp by night—oh God, those hands, those hands, those hands…  

Spoil me a little, the way you do,  
Extra whip on my drink and your hoodie too,  
It’s the way that you show up everywhere—yeah, everywhere.  

[Bridge – Line-by-line blend]  
Slip between pink satin sheets, cool and slick against my skin,  
I shake off the day, let the wild wind win.  
Sweet on my tongue, slow on the trust, silk and citrus, careful lust,  
You pull me close on this dirt‑road kitchen floor, we want less, we’re getting more.  

He doesn’t drown in fantasy, he builds a bridge to get to me,  
Says I’m fire, says I shine, tastes the edges of every line,  
You say “Babe, you been working too hard,” turn the lights down, lock the door,  
From rough rocks outside my door to pink satin sheets and a caramel war.  

[Final Chorus – Big Mash]  
Spoil me a little, it feels so good,  
You know every craving better than I could,

Verse 1
The door hit the wall, the night split wide
Fear on the floor, nowhere to hide
Promises broke like glass in my hands
I learned to survive when no one would stand
I held my breath, I held my ground
While silence screamed the loudest sound

Pre-Chorus
They wrote me down in black and white
But never asked me how I fight

Chorus
I’m still standing, though I’m tired to the bone
Twelve years walking this road alone
They only saw my cracks, my scars
Never saw the way I love so hard
You tried to take what I’d die to defend
I am her mother — I won’t bend
I’m still standing, misunderstood
But I know my heart, and I know it’s good yet we still climbing

Verse 2
I asked for help, they judged my pain
Turned my truth into something shameful again
Every flaw they held like a loaded gun
Ignored the things I’ve always done
I walked into rooms already condemned
While smiling faces sharpened pens

Pre-Chorus
They called it care, they called it concern
But never felt the fire I burn

Chorus
I’m still standing, through the gaslight haze
Labeled, filed, reduced to mistakes
They never wrote the nights I stayed
Never wrote the love I gave
You tried to steal her with words and fear
But a mother’s love is louder than years
I’m still standing, bruised but true
If you knew my heart, you’d know it too
Yet we still climbing 
Bridge
I’m not perfect — I never claimed to be
But I showed up every time she needed me
If strength is measured by who stays
Then I’ve earned my name a thousand ways

(soft)
I fought systems, lies, and shame
But I never stopped saying her name

Chorus (Final)
I’m still standing, even when I break
Even when my hands still shake
You don’t get to rewrite my soul
Or turn my love into a role
I’m more than reports, more than blame
More than someone else’s frame
I’m still standing — hear me say
I chose my child, every day yet we still climbing

Having faith everything is working out as I can slowly see legit everything so far is going our way now which Greatful for ❤️🙏❤️I think we are going to be left alone when those spiritual people say your back is covered etc I’m learning as difficult as the road is we really do have protection as God goes as far as canceling appointments of bad companies  my faith in God is the only way i have got through all this shit thrown our way Amen

Outro
One day she’ll know who held the line
Who chose her, every single time
And when the truth finally gets its turn
They’ll hear my song — and they’ll learn

God I praise and thankyou 
We still climbing

**STRAWBERRY MILK AT THE HOSPITAL** ☕😆
*(Coffeebreak hospital song)*

**[Intro]**
Her: Met a nice dude at the hospital.
Him and his partner. Pretty sure they were together.
Don’t think there were three patients.
They just… knew each other. Anyway lol.

**[Verse 1]**
He looked at me like he’d seen me before.
I was like “sir I don’t think I know you
unless you’ve been in my comments at 2am.”
Then we all got on the scales
like a weird group activity.
They were cool.
10/10 hospital strangers.
Would weigh again.

**[Chorus]**
Tiny sip of the energy drink,
heart stay in your lane.
They said my rate’s as high
as someone with a lung clot.
So I’m cutting back like a responsible adult
who still brought the can in her bag.
Tiny sip. Big personality.
Coffee break. Don’t race. ☕

**[Verse 2]**
They gave me strawberry milk.
I looked at it like it personally insulted me.
Why would you hand me that. I hate it.
So I gave it to Darko.
She goes “they can’t know you hate it.”
I’m like SHHH take the milk.
You like it.
You’re the venter.
You’re the corrector of venting.
You’re now the official strawberry milk disposal unit.
You’re welcome.

**[Bridge]**
Weighed ourselves in a line.
Heart doing too much.
Milk I didn’t ask for.
Darko saving the day.
Hospital’s a strange little stage
and somehow I’m still the host.

**[Final Chorus]**
Tiny sip of the energy drink,
heart stay in your lane.
Strawberry milk in Darko’s hands,
scales and strangers who were cool.
He thought he recognised me.
I said I don’t think so.
Coffee break at the hospital.
Would weigh again. ☕😆

**[Outro]**
Her: Still cutting back?
Her: Yeah. Tiny sip.
Her: Still hate the milk?
Her: Gave it to Darko.
Her: Still funny?
Her: Always.
Both: Coffee break. Don’t race. ☕

A tiny mark from a hospital night,
A cannula once rested there,
While you stayed close and held me tight.
Sweat glistening on our skin,
your kiss tasting the salt of the night.
Close enough to breathe each other in,
lips meeting softly, slowly—
a little heat, a little sweetness,
and the wild taste of summer between us. 💋🌹

Through all the beeping, through all the fear,
You were the sweetest thing I knew,
That little mark may fade away,
But I’ll remember being cared for by you.

So here’s to healing, here’s to love,
To every tear we made it through,
The bruise will disappear someday,
But my heart will remember you. I remember that hospital night,
The soft lights glowing through the room,
A little cannula in my arm,
And somehow love began to bloom.

There was a bruise where it had been,
A tiny reminder left behind,
But sweeter than the mark itself
Were all the gentle moments I find.

The quiet talks, the caring hands,
The little smiles that made me stay,
The feeling that I wasn't alone
Through every long and restless day.

And when I look back now,
I don't just remember fear—
I remember being cared for,
And knowing someone precious was near.
Sweet little vampires came out at night,
Dancing in shadows beneath the moonlight.
They whispered softly, “Don't be afraid,”
And watched over dreams while the night slowly faded.
He leaned over me beneath the silver moon,
His shadow surrounding me like a velvet cloak.
His hands were gentle against my warm skin,
Drawing me closer until I could feel his heartbeat.
Under the pale moon, the two vampire lovers stood impossibly close,
their eyes locked in a silence deeper than words.

He wrapped his arms around her, drawing her gently against him,
while she rested her hands against his chest.
They moved together slowly, as though the whole night had stopped
just to give them this moment.

Their foreheads touched, their breaths mingling in the cool darkness.
He brushed a strand of hair from her face,
and she smiled before pulling him into a tender kiss.

Around them, the candles flickered and the curtains danced in the night breeze.
Two immortal hearts, finding something wonderfully human in each other. 🌙🧛‍♂️❤️🧛‍♀️

His touch was soft, almost impossibly tender,
And his eyes held mine in the darkness.
He whispered my name like a secret,
Pulling me safely into his embrace.

Outside, the night belonged to the vampires—
But in his arms, the darkness felt strangely sweet. 🧛‍♂️🌙❤️

Tiny little fangs and hearts full of care,
Floating like shadows through cool midnight air.
No need to be frightened, no need to hide,
The sweetest little vampires were right by my side. 🧛‍♀️🌙❤️

That little bruise will fade away,
Like every hospital scar,
But the sweetest part of that memory
Will stay exactly where you are. ❤️
